target.title: Fix silent context-engine maintenance task delivery status
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where fast, silent context-engine turn maintenance created a deliverable background-task flow even though it completed without a user-facing message. Those unnecessary one-task flows could remain in task status and flow surfaces after routine maintenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Silent maintenance now starts with delivery marked not applicable, so fast completion keeps only its task audit record and skips one-task-flow creation. If maintenance runs longer than ten seconds or fails, the existing task is promoted through the canonical queued-task path; that restores pending delivery and creates the synchronized one-task flow before any visible progress or failure notification.

## User Impact

Routine fast context maintenance stays silent without cluttering task-flow surfaces. Long-running maintenance still reports progress and completion, and failed maintenance still reports its error with a normal flow handle.

## Evidence

- Sanitized direct AWS Crabbox (`provider=aws`, `cbx_46f531263e30`, run `run_8721baa14e79`) on final head `493cde8831e48666888659504ac94ec6c76e9312`: 86/86 focused tests passed across context-engine maintenance, task executor, task commands, and CLI routing; targeted oxfmt and oxlint also passed.
- The deterministic maintenance fixture covers fast success with no flow or message, greater-than-ten-second progress plus successful flow completion, and quick failure with a failed flow.
- Fresh isolated autoreview on final head `493cde8831e48666888659504ac94ec6c76e9312`: clean, confidence 0.98.
- Exact-head hosted CI: [run 29024771937](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29024771937).
